newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cuts discount rate to 6.25 percent from 6.75 percent.
newsitem.headline: Italy cuts discount rate to 6.25 percent from 6.75 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Italy Friday cut the official discount rate to 6.25 percent from 6.75 percent, effective Monday.
A statement said the bank's fixed-term advances, or Lombard rate, was simultaneously cut to 7.75 percent from 8.25 percent.
The central bank has now cut rates four times since July 1996. The last change to the discount rate was Jan. 21, when it was reduced by three quarters of a perentage point.
The rate cut will come as a relief to the government, which is desperate to lower the interest bill on its debt mountain.

The government estimates that it saves 20 trillion lire ($12 billion) a year in debt servicing costs for every percentage point fall in the discount rate, once the cut has fully worked its way into the system.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who has staked his political career on Italy being a member of the single European currency from the planned Jan. 1, 1999, start, has been saying for the last month that all conditions were in place for a reduction in interest rates.
